q-70807.name: Question 1
q-70807.problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(1,-1,1)$ and is perpendicular to the line 
$\frac{x-2}{-1}=\frac{y-1}{2}=\frac{z+1}{1}.$
q-70807.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨1,-1,1⟩.$ From the canonical equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector $⟨-1,2,1⟩.$ So, the normal vector of the plane is 

$$
n=⟨-1,2,1⟩.
$$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-1,2,1⟩ & =⟨1,-1,1⟩\cdot ⟨-1,2,1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-1,2,1⟩ & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-1,2,1⟩ & =-2 \\ -x+2y+z & =-2 \\ -x+2y+z+2 & =0 \\ x-2y-z-2 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

q-70807.html:
Question 1
?

Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point P(1,−1,1) and is perpendicular to the line x−2−1=y−12=z+11.

a
x−2y−z−2=0
b
x−y+z−5=0
c
−x−2y−z−5=0
d
x−2y−z−5=0
e
x−y+z−2=0
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we note that the position vector of P is p=⟨1,−1,1⟩. From the canonical equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector ⟨−1,2,1⟩. So, the normal vector of the plane is

n=⟨−1,2,1⟩.

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

(r−p)⋅n=0r⋅n=p⋅nr⋅⟨−1,2,1⟩=⟨1,−1,1⟩⋅⟨−1,2,1⟩r⋅⟨−1,2,1⟩=−2

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute r=⟨x,y,z⟩ into the equation above and get

⟨x,y,z⟩⋅⟨−1,2,1⟩=−2−x+2y+z=−2−x+2y+z+2=0x−2y−z−2=0.

q-128380.name: Question 2
q-128380.problem: Given the Cartesian equation $4x+4y-2z=0$ of the plane $Π$, find an equation of $Π$ in the form $(r-p)\cdot n=0.$
q-128380.worked_solution:
First, from the equation of the plane we get that the normal vector of $Π$ is $n=⟨4,4,-2⟩.$

Now, we solve the Cartesian equation of $Π$ for $z$:

$$
\begin{aligned}4x+4y-2z & =0 \\ 2z & =4x+4y \\ z & =2x+2y.\end{aligned}
$$

If we put, say, $x=0$ and $y=0$, we get $z=0.$ Hence, the point $P(0,0,0)$ lies on $Π.$ Note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨0,0,0⟩.$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ (r-⟨0,0,0⟩)\cdot ⟨4,4,-2⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2

Given the Cartesian equation 4x+4y−2z=0 of the plane Π, find an equation of Π in the form (r−p)⋅n=0.

a
(r−⟨0,0,−2⟩)⋅⟨−4,4,−2⟩=0
b
(r−⟨0,0,1⟩)⋅⟨2,4,−4⟩=0
c
(r−⟨0,0,0⟩)⋅⟨4,−2,4⟩=0
d
(r−⟨0,0,2⟩)⋅⟨4,4,2⟩=0
e
(r−⟨0,0,0⟩)⋅⟨4,4,−2⟩=0
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, from the equation of the plane we get that the normal vector of Π is n=⟨4,4,−2⟩.

Now, we solve the Cartesian equation of Π for z: 4x+4y−2z=02z=4x+4yz=2x+2y. If we put, say, x=0 and y=0, we get z=0. Hence, the point P(0,0,0) lies on Π. Note that the position vector of P is p=⟨0,0,0⟩.

Finally, we obtain (r−p)⋅n=0(r−⟨0,0,0⟩)⋅⟨4,4,−2⟩=0.

q-128459.name: Question 3
q-128459.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the points $A(1,-2,0)$, $P(3,-4,1)$ and $Q(2,1,-2).$
q-128459.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $A,P$ and $Q$ are $a=⟨1,-2,0⟩,\,p=⟨3,-4,1⟩,$ and $q=⟨2,1,-2⟩.$

First, using the $3$ points we build $2$ vectors parallel to the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{1} & =\overset{\to }{AP} \\  & =⟨3,-4,1⟩-⟨1,-2,0⟩ \\  & =⟨2,-2,1⟩ \\ {v}_{2} & =\overset{\to }{AQ} \\  & =⟨2,1,-2⟩-⟨1,-2,0⟩ \\  & =⟨1,3,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we need to find the normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={v}_{1}\times {v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & -2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & -2\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =i+5j+8k \\  & =⟨1,5,8⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨1,5,8⟩ & =⟨3,-4,1⟩\cdot ⟨1,5,8⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨1,5,8⟩ & =-9\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨1,5,8⟩ & =-9 \\ x+5y+8z & =-9 \\ x+5y+8z+9 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that the position vectors of the points A,P and Q are a=⟨1,−2,0⟩,p=⟨3,−4,1⟩, and q=⟨2,1,−2⟩.

First, using the 3 points we build 2 vectors parallel to the plane: v1=AP→=⟨3,−4,1⟩−⟨1,−2,0⟩=⟨2,−2,1⟩v2=AQ→=⟨2,1,−2⟩−⟨1,−2,0⟩=⟨1,3,−2⟩

Now, we need to find the normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of v1 and v2 as follows:

n=v1×v2=[2−21]×[13−2]=ijk2−2113−2=i+5j+8k=⟨1,5,8⟩

Then, using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane:

(r−p)⋅n=0r⋅n=p⋅nr⋅⟨1,5,8⟩=⟨3,−4,1⟩⋅⟨1,5,8⟩r⋅⟨1,5,8⟩=−9

Finally, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute r=⟨x,y,z⟩ into the equation above and get

⟨x,y,z⟩⋅⟨1,5,8⟩=−9x+5y+8z=−9x+5y+8z+9=0.

q-330576.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨7,4,-3⟩.$ From the canonical equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector $⟨5,4,-2⟩.$ So, the normal vector of the plane is 

$$
n=⟨5,4,-2⟩.

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨5,4,-2⟩ & =⟨7,4,-3⟩\cdot ⟨5,4,-2⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨5,4,-2⟩ & =57\end{aligned}

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get
